title: A flat hypersurface lowers Cohen–Macaulay fibre local dimension by one
statement: Let $g:Y\to S$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $s\in S$ and let $y$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] of the scheme-theoretic fibre $Y_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y_s,y}$, and write $\mathfrak n$ for its maximal ideal. Suppose $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $d=\dim A$ is a finite integer with $d>0$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. There exist an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ of the image of $y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] and an element $a\in B$ such that its germ $h\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ lies in the maximal ideal and its image $\bar h\in A$ lies in $\mathfrak n$ and is a nonzerodivisor (multiplication by $\bar h$ on $A$ is injective). The closed subscheme $D=\operatorname{Spec}(B/(a))\hookrightarrow U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] has a closed point $y_D\in D_s$ mapping to $y$. The composite $D\to U\to Y\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, and there is an isomorphism of local rings $\mathcal O_{D_s,y_D}\cong A/(\bar h)$ compatible with the maps from $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. In particular $\mathcal O_{D_s,y_D}$ is Noetherian of dimension $d-1$ and depth at least $d-1$.

proof.text: Let $x$ be the image of $y$ under $Y_s\to Y$; then $g(x)=s$. The fibre-stalk theorem identifies its designated unique point above $x$ with the given $y$, and gives a surjection $R=\mathcal O_{Y,x}\twoheadrightarrow A$. As a module over itself, $A$ is generated by $1$, so the finite-module depth definition applies. The stalk $A$ is a nonzero local ring, and $\mathfrak n A=\mathfrak n\ne A$, so the exceptional infinite-depth clause for $IM=M$ does not apply. Since $d>0$ and $\operatorname{depth}A\ge d$, the supremum clause of the depth definition supplies an $A$-regular sequence in $\mathfrak n$ of positive length: if all lengths were zero their supremum would be zero. Let $\bar h$ be its first element. The regular-sequence definition says multiplication by $\bar h$ on $A$ is injective. Lift $\bar h$ through the displayed surjection to $h\in R$. This lift lies in the maximal ideal of $R$: otherwise it would be a unit, whose image would be a unit in $A$, contradicting $\bar h\in\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, positive-dimensional case; Tag 056Z, lemma-slice-once; Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element.

proof.text: Apply the fibre-regular-element flat-hypersurface theorem to $g:Y\to S$, the point $x\in Y$ from step 1, and this germ $h$. Its hypotheses are local finite presentation, flatness at this point (implied by the assumed flatness of $g$), $h$ in the maximal ideal, and injectivity of multiplication by its fibre image, established in step 1. Obtain $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $a\in B$ with germ $h$, and $D=\operatorname{Spec}(B/(a))\hookrightarrow U$ containing $x$. The theorem gives flatness and local finite presentation of the composite $D\to S$.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, positive-dimensional case; Tag 056Z, lemma-slice-once; Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element.

proof.text: Apply the proved principal-hypersurface fibre-stalk theorem to the affine chart and section obtained in step 2. The germ image is precisely $\bar h$, already in the fibre maximal ideal. It supplies a closed point $y_D$ above $y$ and an isomorphism from the new fibre stalk to $A/(\bar h)$ with the required compatibility from $\mathcal O_{Y,x}$. This proves the former steps 3 and 4 by the quotient universal property, without ideal-sheaf tensor images or localization of quotients.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, positive-dimensional case: the assertion O_{D_s,x} = O_{X_s,x}/(hbar); Schemes Tags 01JU and 0HA1; Algebra Tag 00CT.

proof.text: Injectivity of multiplication by $\bar h$ puts it in the nonzerodivisors of $A$. Apply depth_quotient_nonzerodivisor to obtain Noetherianity, dimension $d-1$, and a regular sequence of length $d-1$ in the quotient maximal ideal. Transport Noetherianity and Krull dimension along the displayed ring equivalence. Map that regular sequence through its inverse ring equivalence: AddEquiv.isRegular_congr preserves regularity, and map_ringEquiv_maximalIdeal preserves membership in the maximal ideal. Its unchanged length contributes to the supremum defining depth, proving the desired lower bound even for $d=1$, where the list is empty. Combine these with steps 1--3.
